author: cc-t3
source_runs: benchmark/2026-09-30-r17p-{5ea,61b}-sweep (r17p full-66, both boards); raw dlopen lines from <app>/hilog.txt
question: outer loop: for the 4 dlopen_ns native apps, is the fix JAR-layer (classloader->namespace mapping, cc-t3) or native-loader (cx-t0)? Table first, then act.

decisive_source_fact.finding: BuildAppConfig (lines 64-90) reads the app's library_path AND permitted_path as JStrings passed from Java, and splits them into app_search_paths / app_permitted_paths. Only bridge_search_paths/bridge_permitted_paths come from the C++ policy (OwnPolicy(kBridge*)). So the app namespace's search+permitted paths ARE Java-supplied.
decisive_source_fact.but: Grepping the runtime-JAR Java sources (bms/src/adapter/framework/*/java) for anyone building that library_path/permitted_path string returns ONLY B7BindFixes.java -- and that is createNativeNamespace for the RUNTIME classloader (the WESTLAKE .so namespace), NOT the app's. No Java class in oh-adapter-runtime.jar assembles the APP's library_path/permitted_path; that string is built by native-loader-oh / appspawn-x (native).
decisive_source_fact.corroborating_error: fd-client hilog: 'UnsatisfiedLinkError: path is outside app domain: /system/android/lib64/libwestlake_html_compat.so' == a permitted-paths rejection, which is enforced by native-loader-oh, not the runtime JAR.

apps.raw: dlopen_ns failed for .../libgdx.so: Error loading shared library libstdc++.so: (needed by .../libgdx.so)
apps.why_not_found: libstdc++.so lives in /system/android/lib64 (a kBridge-searchable dir) but is NOT a kBridgeSharedSoname, so the bridge does not expose it to the app namespace; and the app's own search+permitted paths do not include it as a resolvable soname.
apps.layer: native (app search/permitted paths are native-built; fix = add libstdc++.so to kBridgeSharedSonames, or add /system/android/lib64 to the app path in native-loader-oh/appspawn-x) -> cx-t0
apps.jar_angle: SPECULATIVE: reflectively append /system/android/lib64 to the app library_path+permitted_path before native createClassloaderNamespace. Not confirmed; no JAR class currently builds that string.

apps.raw: dlopen_ns failed for .../libarc.so: Error loading shared library libOpenSLES.so: (needed by .../libarc.so)
apps.why_not_found: libOpenSLES.so is in /system/lib64, which is in NEITHER the app namespace search/permitted paths NOR kBridgeSearchPaths/kBridgePermittedPaths, and it is not a shared soname. Unreachable from the app namespace.
apps.layer: native (add /system/lib64 to kBridgeSearchPaths+kBridgePermittedPaths + libOpenSLES.so soname, OR to the app path builder in native-loader-oh/appspawn-x) -> cx-t0
apps.jar_angle: SPECULATIVE: same as fd-app (append /system/lib64 to the app path). Not confirmed.

apps.raw_dlopen: dlopen_ns failed for .../libconscrypt_jni.so: Error loading shared library liblog.so: (needed by .../libconscrypt_jni.so)
apps.raw_fatal: Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException: Parameter specified as non-null is null: method com.nextcloud.client.mixins.SessionMixin.<init>, parameter accountManager -> Unable to start activity ComponentInfo{com.nextcloud.client/com.nmc.android.ui.LauncherActivity}
apps.why_not_found: liblog.so is both bridge-searchable and a shared soname yet still 'not found' for conscrypt -- points to a namespace-link gap (native-loader-oh), not a path the JAR sets.
apps.lit_blocker: NOT the dlopen. The activity crash is an app-internal DI NPE (accountManager null in SessionMixin), same family as fd-reader. So fixing conscrypt's liblog would NOT light fd-client.
apps.layer: conscrypt/liblog = native namespace-link (cx-t0); lit-blocker = app-internal (parked, not JAR)

apps.missing_dep: n/a -- SYMBOL/RELOCATION error, not 'library not found'. The .so is reached but a symbol it needs is unresolved.
apps.why_not_found: ABI/symbol mismatch (unsupported symbol), independent of search/permitted paths.
apps.layer: native ABI/symbol -> cx-t0. A path fix cannot help a relocation error.

verdict: None of the 4 is a runtime-JAR classloader->namespace fix that cc-t3 owns today: the app namespace's library_path/permitted_path is built in native-loader-oh/appspawn-x (no Java class in oh-adapter-runtime.jar assembles it), the missing sonames/paths are governed by the C++ kBridge policy, fd-im-vector is a native relocation error, and fd-client's lit-blocker is an app-internal NPE. Route the dlopen/namespace half to cx-t0 (native-loader-oh).
discriminating_experiment_if_JAR_angle_p: Reflectively append '/system/lib64:/system/android/lib64' to the app library_path AND permitted_path just before the native createClassloaderNamespace call (intercept ApplicationLoaders/LoadedApk from the runtime JAR). Re-run mindustry (libOpenSLES exists in /system/lib64) and fd-app (libstdc++ exists in /system/android/lib64). If both load their deps -> a JAR increment is viable after all. If they still fail with 'path is outside app domain'/'not found' -> the path is native-built and the fix is cx-t0's. This is a hypothesis, NOT an attribution.
